## Purpose

Create the implementation task only after Jack approves an issue investigation
report. See the [triage guide](../../guides/github-issue-triage.md).

## When a playbook uses it

The `file-approved-fix` rule calls it for an `approve` `review.decided` event.

## How it works internally

`GitHubIssueCommandsMixin._cmd_github_issue_fix_approved` in
`src/commands/github_issue_commands.py` verifies that the review belongs to
an issue investigation and that the event names its current approved revision.
It reads that report and files a fix task whose instructions require `Fixes #N`
in the PR body.

## Side effects and persistence

The fix task uses a key containing the issue number and review ID. A replay
returns `reused` with the same task ID, even after the task is archived.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

An unrelated review or stale event returns `ignored`. Invalid project input,
a missing approved revision, or task filing failure returns `rejected` and
fails the playbook run. Inspect the run with `aq playbook show-run <run-id>`.

## Example step

The `file-approved-fix` rule passes the event's `project_id`, `review_id`, and
`revision` to `github_issue_fix_approved`. `created`, `reused`, and `ignored`
complete the rule.
